story.title: Macedonia now brings in the most revenue

explain.duplicates: Remove Duplicates with every column ticked removes O1034's and O1121's second copies (rows 36 and 124). `=COUNTIF(A:A,A2)` shows 2 for both before you do.
explain.blanks: O1057 and O1098 have no region. Both belong to Giorgos Nikolaou, whose home region is Macedonia: `=VLOOKUP(E2,$Q$2:$R$8,2,FALSE)` filled into the blanks only.
explain.region-text: ` attica `, `CRETE` and `crete`: `=TRIM(PROPER(D2))` filled down D (pasted as values) gives Attica, Crete, Crete.
explain.quantities: O1045 ("14") and O1150 ("1") are text: Convert to Number on column G, or `=VALUE(G2)`.
explain.typo-and-date: O1088's `P0O2` → `P002` (Find & Replace, column C, match entire cell). O1170's 2026-12-12 → 2025-12-12.
explain.pivot: Rows: Region; Columns: Date grouped by Quarters; Values: Sum of Revenue; inserted after cleaning (or refreshed after the last move). A pivot built on the raw export and never refreshed keeps the old, wrong totals.
explain.chart: A column (or bar) chart of the Qtr4 series, largest first, with Macedonia highlighted and named in the title. A line would suggest a trend between regions; a pie can't be compared across five slices.
explain.insight: Qtr4: Macedonia 48,781.8 ÷ Qtr4 total 113,802.5 = 42.9%. Attica leads the full year (124,579.85) but only brought in 17,139.75 in Qtr4: the slide's real message is that the business now depends on Macedonia.
